Tehran official had promised ‘decisive and painful’ reply to Israeli bombing of apartment buildings in Beirut’s southern suburbs Iran launched missiles at Israel on Sunday in response to Israeli strikes on Beirut’s southern suburbs, shattering a fragile ceasefire and marking the most serious escalation since April, after 100 days of war. A senior Iranian official has promised a “decisive and painful” response to Israel’s airstrikes on the southern suburbs of Beirut and, a few hours later, sirens sounded across northern Israel. The Israel Defense Forces said it had so far intercepted all the Iranian ballistic missiles, as US president Donald Trump called Israeli prime minister Bejamin Netanyahu urging him ‘‘not to strike back, adding he was ‘‘not happy about it’’ and that it would “not help” negotiations with Tehran.

See more of our coverage in your search results. Iran bombarded Israel with missiles Sunday in the first major attack since last week’s delicate cease-fire, defying US orders to stand down and endangering the fragile peace. Sirens sounded in several parts of the Jewish state as its military began attempts to intercept at least three barrages of missiles, with Israel warning that its defense wasn’t iron-clad. There were no immediate reports of casualties or major damage, but the country is still bracing for more strikes, the New York Times reported. Mohsen Rezaei, an adviser to Iran’s supreme leader, appeared to claim responsibility for the strikes on social media — with the attack coming hours after Israel struck Beirut’s southern suburbs, aiming for the Iranian-allied Hezbollah terror group there.

On Sunday night, the IDF said missiles had been launched from Iran towards Israel and it was also preparing for attacks after its Beirut strike. Iran launched about 10 ballistic missiles at northern Israel. All the missiles were intercepted or struck open areas, according to the military. Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said: “This operation is not a passing event, but rather the beginning of a full week of continuous strikes.” In a statement it added: “Waves of missiles and drones will continue to be launched around the clock for the next seven days until the enemy is deterred and ceases its crimes. “Any targeting of Iranian territory will be met with a devastating and overwhelming response beyond all expectation.”

[Lähde: The Guardian World]
Tehran official had promised ‘decisive and painful’ reply to Israeli bombing of apartment buildings in Beirut’s southern suburbs

Iran launched missiles at Israel on Sunday in response to Israeli strikes on Beirut’s southern suburbs, shattering a fragile ceasefire and marking the most serious escalation since April, after 100 days of war.

A senior Iranian official has promised a “decisive and painful” response to Israel’s airstrikes on the southern suburbs of Beirut and, a few hours later, sirens sounded across northern Israel.

The Israel Defense Forces said it had so far intercepted all the Iranian ballistic missiles, as US president Donald Trump called Israeli prime minister Bejamin Netanyahu urging him ‘‘not to strike back, adding he was ‘‘not happy about it’’ and that it would “not help” negotiations with Tehran.

After the Israeli attack in the Dahieh district of Beirut, Ebrahim Rezaei, the spokesperson for the Iranian parliament’s foreign policy and national security committee, wrote on X: “We will give a decisive and painful response to the Zionist regime’s attack on the suburbs … Watch the sky of the occupied territories tonight.” Iran considers Israel to be occupied Palestine.

The speaker of Iran’s parliament and top negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said US bases and assets in the region had become “legitimate targets” after the Israeli strike.

“They are neither committed to a ceasefire nor believe in dialogue, and through the naval blockade and violation of agreements regarding Lebanon they showed that they only understand the language of power,” Ghalibaf said in a post on X.

On Sunday night, the IDF said missiles had been launched from Iran towards Israel and it was also preparing for attacks after its Beirut strike.

Iran launched about 10 ballistic missiles at northern Israel.

All the missiles were intercepted or struck open areas, according to the military.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said: “This operation is not a passing event, but rather the beginning of a full week of continuous strikes.”

In a statement it added: “Waves of missiles and drones will continue to be launched around the clock for the next seven days until the enemy is deterred and ceases its crimes.

“Any targeting of Iranian territory will be met with a devastating and overwhelming response beyond all expectation.”

---

[Lähde: New York Post]
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Iran bombarded Israel with missiles Sunday in the first major attack since last week’s delicate cease-fire, defying US orders to stand down and endangering the fragile peace.

Sirens sounded in several parts of the Jewish state as its military began attempts to intercept at least three barrages of missiles, with Israel warning that its defense wasn’t iron-clad.

There were no immediate reports of casualties or major damage, but the country is still bracing for more strikes, the New York Times reported.

Mohsen Rezaei, an adviser to Iran’s supreme leader, appeared to claim responsibility for the strikes on social media — with the attack coming hours after Israel struck Beirut’s southern suburbs, aiming for the Iranian-allied Hezbollah terror group there.

“Tonight, the aggressors received their response,” Rezaei wrote, adding that Israel would see “a more crushing response and heavier costs” if it retaliates.

Iran’s state broadcasters also confirmed the launches, saying that “if Israel responds to Iranian attacks or does not stop its attacks on Lebanon, Iranian attacks will continue.”

US officials have repeatedly cautioned Israel against escalating the war as they try to broker a permanent deal with Iran. Israel claimed its attack on Beirut was also retaliation for Hezbollah.

Last week, Lebanese and Israeli governments agreed to a ceasefire, but Hezbollah rejected the deal. Pakistan is also trying to revive talks between Tehran and Washington with little success as Iran stipulates a deal must include an end to Israel’s war in Lebanon.

Israel has maintained a military presence in Lebanon in pursuit of Hezbollah – a hard-line that has consistently complicated the deal to end the war with Iran.

In NBC’s “Meet The Press” interview that aired on Sunday, President Donald Trump said that he was “not demanding” that Lebanon be part of an overall ceasefire deal.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is up for reelection later this year, has insisted on pressing ahead with Israel’s offense in Lebanon until he believes Hezbollah no longer poses a threat.

Before the strikes in Beirut, Iran warned an attack would spark a full-scale war across the Middle East.

payload.title: Iran laukaisi ohjuksia Israeliin Beirutin iskujen jälkeen
payload.summary: Iran laukaisi sunnuntaina ohjuksia Israeliin vastauksena Israelin iskuihin Beirutin eteläisiin esikaupunkeihin. Israelin armeijan mukaan ohjuksia torjuttiin, eikä välittömistä uhreista tai laajoista vahingoista kerrottu.
payload.content:
Iran laukaisi sunnuntaina ohjuksia kohti Israelia sen jälkeen, kun Israel oli iskenyt Beirutin eteläisiin esikaupunkeihin. Iskut rikkoivat hauraan tulitauon ja merkitsivät vakavinta kärjistymistä sitten huhtikuun noin sadan päivän sodan jälkeen. Hälytyssireenit soivat Pohjois-Israelissa ja useilla muilla alueilla, kun Israelin armeija aloitti Iranista laukaistujen ohjusten torjunnan.

## Ohjuksia kohti Pohjois-Israelia

Israelin puolustusvoimien mukaan Iran laukaisi sunnuntai-iltana ohjuksia kohti Israelia. Armeijan mukaan kyse oli noin kymmenestä ballistisesta ohjuksesta, jotka joko torjuttiin tai putosivat avoimille alueille. Toisessa lähdetiedossa kuvattiin ainakin kolmea ohjusaaltoa, joiden aikana sireenit soivat eri puolilla Israelia.

Välittömiä tietoja uhreista tai merkittävistä vahingoista ei ollut. Israel kuitenkin varoitti, ettei sen puolustus ole aukoton, ja maa varautui mahdollisiin uusiin iskuihin. Israelin armeija kertoi myös valmistautuvansa hyökkäyksiin sen jälkeen, kun se oli tehnyt iskun Beirutiin.

## Beirutin isku taustalla

Ohjusisku seurasi Israelin iskuja Beirutin eteläisiin esikaupunkeihin. Lähdetietojen mukaan Israel kohdisti iskut alueella toimivaan Iranin tukemaan Hizbollahiin. Teheranista oli jo ennen ohjuslaukaisuja annettu viesti, jonka mukaan Israelin toimiin vastattaisiin ratkaisevasti ja kivuliaasti.

Iranin ylimmän johtajan neuvonantaja Mohsen Rezaei näytti ottavan vastuuta iskuista sosiaalisessa mediassa. Hyökkäys kuvattiin ensimmäiseksi suureksi iskuksi viime viikon herkän tulitauon jälkeen, mikä lisäsi huolta siitä, että jo valmiiksi hauras rauhoittuminen voi murtua nopeasti.

## Tulitauko horjuu

Iranin vallankumouskaarti kuvasi operaatiota alkuvaiheeksi eikä yksittäiseksi tapahtumaksi. Sen mukaan ohjus- ja droonihyökkäyksiä voitaisiin jatkaa ympäri vuorokauden viikon ajan, kunnes vastapuoli lopettaa Iranin mukaan rikoksensa. Vallankumouskaarti varoitti myös, että Iranin alueeseen kohdistuviin iskuihin vastattaisiin erittäin voimakkaasti.

Yhdysvaltain presidentti Donald Trump oli lähdetietojen mukaan yhteydessä Israelin pääministeriin Bejamin Netanjahuun ja kehotti tätä olemaan iskemättä takaisin. Trumpin kerrottiin sanoneen, ettei vastaisku auttaisi neuvotteluja Teheranin kanssa. Tilanne jäi epävarmaksi: Israel kertoi torjuneensa tähänastiset ohjukset, mutta Iranin lausunnot viittasivat mahdollisiin uusiin iskuihin.
summary_bullets: Iran laukaisi sunnuntaina ohjuksia kohti Israelia Beirutin eteläisiin esikaupunkeihin tehtyjen iskujen jälkeen.
Israelin armeijan mukaan noin kymmenen ballistista ohjusta torjuttiin tai ne putosivat avoimille alueille.
Välittömiä tietoja uhreista tai merkittävistä vahingoista ei ollut.
Iranin vallankumouskaarti varoitti mahdollisista uusista ohjus- ja drooni-iskuista.

Tilanne jäi epävarmaksi: Israel kertoi torjuneensa tähänastiset ohjukset, mutta Iranin lausunnot viittasivat mahdollisiin uusiin iskuihin.

Tehran official had promised ‘decisive and painful’ reply to Israeli bombing of apartment buildings in Beirut’s southern suburbs Iran launched missiles at Israel on Sunday in response to Israeli strikes on Beirut’s southern suburbs, shattering a fragile ceasefire and marking the most serious escalation since April, after 100 days of war. A senior Iranian official has promised a “decisive and painful” response to Israel’s airstrikes on the southern suburbs of Beirut and, a few hours later, sirens sounded across northern Israel. The Israel Defense Forces said it had so far intercepted all the Iranian ballistic missiles, as US president Donald Trump called Israeli prime minister Bejamin Netanyahu urging him ‘‘not to strike back, adding he was ‘‘not happy about it’’ and that it would “not help” negotiations with Tehran.

See more of our coverage in your search results. Iran bombarded Israel with missiles Sunday in the first major attack since last week’s delicate cease-fire, defying US orders to stand down and endangering the fragile peace. Sirens sounded in several parts of the Jewish state as its military began attempts to intercept at least three barrages of missiles, with Israel warning that its defense wasn’t iron-clad. There were no immediate reports of casualties or major damage, but the country is still bracing for more strikes, the New York Times reported. Mohsen Rezaei, an adviser to Iran’s supreme leader, appeared to claim responsibility for the strikes on social media — with the attack coming hours after Israel struck Beirut’s southern suburbs, aiming for the Iranian-allied Hezbollah terror group there.

On Sunday night, the IDF said missiles had been launched from Iran towards Israel and it was also preparing for attacks after its Beirut strike. Iran launched about 10 ballistic missiles at northern Israel. All the missiles were intercepted or struck open areas, according to the military. Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said: “This operation is not a passing event, but rather the beginning of a full week of continuous strikes.” In a statement it added: “Waves of missiles and drones will continue to be launched around the clock for the next seven days until the enemy is deterred and ceases its crimes. “Any targeting of Iranian territory will be met with a devastating and overwhelming response beyond all expectation.”
